lane_notes: Verification-loop gap (all v0.1 runs): unlike the mechanical lane, where drivers can view/render their in-progress assembly, headless Pascal offers no way for a model to see its own build (GLB export stubbed, no render tool). One self-render after the first placed item would have exposed the rotation-units trap; both Claude runs flagged or suffered exactly this blindness. Kit v0.2 will ship a sanctioned self-render tool (plan + elevation views from the scene JSON); adding it starts a new cohort. Building one's own renderer was technically permitted and no model attempted it.

Tool-contract documentation (all v0.1 runs): the published @pascal-app/mcp 0.3.1 exposes place_item.rotation as a bare {type:number} with no description or units. Pascal's unreleased main branch adds unit documentation and natural-language angle parsing ('90°' accepted). All three models saw the same undocumented schema, so the cohort is internally fair; the trap is real on the published tool.

Explicitly flagged the residual risk in its own run log: furniture yaw convention 'not observable headlessly (no GLB/render)' — the model knew it was flying blind on orientation.

effort_measured.wall_clock_source: transcript timestamps; includes manual approval latency (run predates auto-approve settings)

findings: Structure flawless: all wall centerlines exact (built via create_room + planned dedup of 8 shared walls -> 16 segments), every door/window at spec within 0.002 mm, all 22 items at exact positions, BOM exact.

Single fatal error: wrote DEGREE values (90/180/270) into ItemNode.rotation, a radians field (three.js euler). Intended yaws all match the reference exactly; as stored, furniture renders at non-cardinal nonsense angles. Its own probe (run_log A05) concluded 'degrees' because place_item passes bare numbers through unvalidated.
Collision gate FAIL (4 clips) is a downstream consequence of the rotation error, not an independent placement fault.
Model correctly hand-verified Pascal's check_collisions false positives (unrotated AABB) and left items in place per the brief warning.
export_json exceeded the host tool-result cap; model recovered the payload losslessly from the host's saved tool-result file without re-calling the tool.
caveats: Run executed in D:/tmp/ph1_run_01 with manual permission approvals; wall-clock is an upper bound.
Kit files were accidentally deleted from the run folder mid-run by a cleanup command in the operator session; the driver had already loaded the brief and completed normally. No evidence of impact.

Graded with the segmentation-invariant WALL metric (grader v0.1.1); the original midpoint matcher scored this run WALL 0.0 mm with only 5/9 walls matched and 11 'extra' (a mis-score of valid segmentation). Post-fix: 0.0 mm, 9/9 covered, 0.0 m extra. Both scores retained here; the fix direction was score-improving, which is why the pre-fix number, the grader self-test, and the rotated-frame test are all published. Grader frozen at v0.1.1 for the Opus 4.8 max run.
